messages:
maya: quick heads-up — after the runtime roll earlier today we're seeing a sustained drop in KV cache hit rate for short-seq requests (p50 seqlen 8-16). metrics: cache_hit_rate went from ~98% -> ~72%. suspect is the new kernel path mapping + key-salting change in the driver. anyone else?

raj: saw the alert. interestingly the long-seq traffic looks unchanged. likely keying mismatch rather than eviction. did the driver flip key namespace or add a version prefix?

maya: driver diff added a `key_version` field and a per-arch salt for kernel-path routing. snippet in the commit: `key = sha256(salt || model_id || session_id || prefix)` — previously we used `model_id||session_id||prefix`. the salt is architecture-specific so same request can map to different keys when routed to different host types.

katie: yikes. that explains why some nodes see misses while others hit. we never persisted salt in the cache index metadata. so cached entries written before deploy will be unreachable.

simon: quick repro idea: take a cached short-seq request from predeploy, compute both key variants and query store. i can run this against the snapshot store. maya, can you paste an example key/req?

maya: here's a sample request trace id 0x9a7f: seqlen 12, model rdx-3b, arch = a100, predeploy key: `rdx-3b|sess-42|pref-gpt`

maya: postdeploy salted key (arch a100) -> `sha256(0x1f3a || rdx-3b|sess-42|pref-gpt) = 0xe4b2...`

cachebot: build-cache-scan report for trace 0x9a7f: predeploy key exists on node 7, postdeploy key not found.

raj: options I see: 1) backfill a mapping from v1->v2 keys during a migration pass (expensive); 2) accept both key formats in lookup for a transition window (cheaper but adds extra latency on misses); 3) roll driver back and do a planned salted rollout with metadata.

katie: prefer option 2 short-term: if we implement dual-key lookup we can restore hit rate quickly while we design a proper migration. need to check perf impact — extra hash and two-store-reads on cold misses.

maya: perf quick numbers: extra sha256 + 1 read adds ~0.6ms p99 on our short-path bench. acceptable if transient. long-term we want a metadata upgrade so persisted blobs include `key_version`. then new lookups compute only v2.

simon: also concerned about model variant switching. Some requests are re-routed to an int8 quant variant; that path uses different kernel selection logic and we added a separate salt per kernel-profile too. that multiplies key variants. we should avoid combinatorial explosion.

katie: agreed — rule: salt only by routing class, not by micro-kernel. maintain one salt per routing policy (latency/cost tier) and store `routing_policy` in cache metadata.

maya: proposed short-term plan: 
- add dual-key lookup in runtime (check v2, then v1) behind a feature flag `kv.dual_lookup=true`.
- emit telemetry tag `kv_lookup_fell_back` when v1 used.
- run for 48h and monitor hit rate and latency.
- meanwhile write a batch migration tool to scan store and emit v2 keys for existing v1 objects (throttle to avoid IO spike).

katie: can take the migration tool. I'll also add a config to persist `key_version` in new writes so we can retire dual lookup after backfill.

raj: tests: we'll need a mixed cluster canary where half nodes have salted writes and dual-lookup enabled. also a chaos test that re-routes a request mid-session to another arch to ensure consistency.

simon: add a watch on cache_hit_rate by seqlen bins (0-8,9-16,17-64) and by routing_policy. if short-seq bins recover to >=95% we can start backfill.

maya: I'll push a small PR with dual lookup and telemetry. PR will include switch and simple benchmarking numbers.

cachebot: deploy-bot: build passed for branch `kv/dual-lookup`; staging deploy queued.

katie: migration tool plan: scan prefix `rdx-*` keys, compute v2 key, write new key with TTL copy, mark `migrated=true` in metadata. will add a dry-run mode that reports counts.

raj: note on TTL semantics — if we copy entries we must preserve remaining TTL. prefer `GET+PUT` that writes with the same remaining TTL. ensure operations are idempotent.

maya: one more gotcha: model reloads that change kernel-path mapping at runtime could still create mismatches if we warm caches on new mapping. we should add a handshake: when driver updates mapping, it broadcasts `mapping_version` and runtime will attach `mapping_version` to writes. lookup will accept keys for current mapping_version and previous N versions (N=1 default).

katie: good call. I'll surface mapping_version in metadata and make migration tool set it to the new version for copied keys.

simon: timeline?

maya: plan: dual-lookup PR today, stag deploy tomorrow, monitor 48h. migration dry-run after 24h if hit rate improved. full backfill over next week.

raj: i'll set up canary and the seqlen/routing dashboards. ping me when staging is up.

maya: thanks all. tagging followups: @katie for migration, @raj for dashboards, @simon for chaos test. :thumbsup:
